Ascribe design candidates

The candidate marks, palettes, and type scales, each in light and dark. The docs pages are the element library's, review's, and the docs site's own stylesheets with the candidate's colors. Contrast is WCAG 2's: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for a bar, border, or mark that carries meaning.

BaselineInkPaper

The marks

Each palette below shows every mark: in one color, in full color with the palette's accent as the second color, at 16, 24, 32, 64, and 128 pixels, and in VS Code's activity bar and a browser tab.

Bracket

A lowercase a with an opening bracket in its margin, like a note's bar or review's change bar: text, and something said about it. The a is drawn from a circle and a stem, so there's no font to license. Weak in that it reads as two letters, "[a", and the bracket alone suggests code more than documents.

design/candidates/mark-bracket.svg

Caret

The proofreader's caret, the mark for "insert here", with a dot: an A, and an edit. It ties the name to review and to writing, reads at 16 pixels as a clear A, and needs no letterforms drawn. Weak where a plain chevron already means "collapse" or "up"; the dot is what tells them apart, and it's small at 16.

design/candidates/mark-caret.svg

Cited

A lowercase a in brackets, as a citation is set: [a]. Closing the bracket turns the Bracket candidate from code into a reference. Weak at 16 pixels, where three shapes crowd one square, and square brackets still say "code" to some.

design/candidates/mark-cited.svg

Double dagger

The double dagger, the footnote mark that sends a reader to the source: ‡. Bold and plain, it holds up at 16 pixels and tints well in the activity bar. Weak because it has nothing of the name in it, and it's close to a plus or a cross at a glance.

design/candidates/mark-dagger.svg

Footnote

A lowercase a with a raised asterisk: a word with a note on it, the plainest sign that something is cited. The a is drawn from a circle and a stem, so there's no font to license, and at 16 pixels the asterisk becomes a spark at the corner. Weak where an asterisk alone means "required" or "new" in forms and toolbars, so the a has to carry it.

design/candidates/mark-footnote.svg

Nib

A pen nib, point down, with its slit: to ascribe is to write something down and say whose it is. A solid shape, so it holds up best of the three at 16 pixels and in a tinted activity bar. Weak because a nib is common: editors, writing apps, and signing tools use one, so it says "writing" more than "Ascribe".

design/candidates/mark-nib.svg

Section

The section sign, the mark that cites a part of a law or a specification: §. Documentation as code is close to a spec, and the sign is rare in software toolbars. In full color the whole sign takes the accent. Weak at 16 pixels, where its loops close up, and some readers will take it for an S.

design/candidates/mark-section.svg

Baseline

Today's values, to compare against. design/candidates/baseline.toml
